findings.title: A policy waiver on a sibling rule now disables the whole scan, withdrawing enforcement nobody exempted
locations: src/Scan.jl:395-397 — apply_ledger, the `enforced` loop
src/Scan.jl:111-112 — rules_for_scan
src/Scan.jl:382-390 — the docstring paragraph that declares the mirror case a known limit
test/scans.jl:166-180 — the new testset, which asserts only the disabling direction
findings.why_it_matters: A consumer that already holds `RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE`, `scope = "policy"`, `target = "*"` in .gbg/exemptions.toml had SCAN.DEAD_REF running before this commit: dead @ref targets were hits and failed the gate. After it, that same untouched ledger entry disables SCAN.DEAD_REF entirely — every hit exempted, `disabled = true` — so RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS, which the consumer never waived, silently stops being enforced. Same shape for RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING → SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE and RULE.CIT.DOI → SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK (the three scans I confirmed have two rules apiece). The gate flips from FAIL to PASS with no line in the scan report saying which rule bought the silence, and no ledger re-read or re-approval is asked of the consumer whose entry now means something larger than it did when it was written.
findings.description: The defect being fixed was real and one-directional: a documented RULE.CIT.DOI waiver resolved against nothing, so it was void. The fix, however, is symmetric — it makes ANY of a scan's rules a master switch for ALL of them — and the diff itself records the consequence as a known limit rather than narrowing it. A waiver could have been made to exempt only the hits of the rule it names (or, failing per-hit attribution, to be refused loudly for a multi-rule scan) instead of silently enlarging the meaning of ledger entries already on disk. The test added in the same commit pins the disabling direction four ways and pins nothing about the sibling rule that loses its enforcement, so the oracle cannot fail on the half that regressed.
findings.evidence: src/Scan.jl:382-390 states it plainly: "The mirror case is NOT fixed and is a known limit: a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted." Computed from policy/RULES.toml `check` arrays: SCAN.DEAD_REF is named by RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS and RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE; SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE by RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API and RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING; SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK by RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE and RULE.CIT.DOI.

findings.title: close refuses every docs round that has no ROUND.toml build record, including every round already open
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:1160-1170 — the new refusal block in close
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:314-326 — build becomes the only writer of rec["build"]
schema/round.schema.json:214-237 — the new `build` object

findings.before:
function build(cfg::AbstractDict, round::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout)
    guard(cfg, round; io)
    log = joinpath(Preflight.scratch_dir(cfg, round), "build.log")
    code = run_under_round(cfg, round, cfg["package"]["docs_build"]; log)
    println(io, "build: exit $code — $log"); return code
findings.after:
if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS
        b = get(rec, "build", nothing)
        if b === nothing
            push!(fails, "no docs build is recorded for this round — gbg round build $round")
findings.why_it_matters: Any check-docs or check-consistency round opened before this commit carries no `build` key — the key did not exist — so `gbg round close` on it now refuses where it would have closed, and the only remedy is an extra full docs build through a verb the session was not previously required to run. The refusal is also not satisfied by the builds the round already ran and already gated on: `prepare` requires exit 0 for both docs instruments and `pass open` rebuilds and refuses a red build for check-consistency (Passes.jl:566-568), yet neither records anything, so a check-consistency round whose every pass was gated on a green build is refused for lack of a record. And because `build` now writes ROUND.toml, satisfying the new gate dirties the round directory, which close's own "the round's files are not committed" check then refuses until a further commit.
findings.description: The defect — a red build riding through graded passes of a check-docs round — is real and worth a gate. The remedy is wider than it: it applies to both docs instruments though only check-docs lacked a re-check, it credits none of the green builds the round already required, and it gives rounds in flight at the moment of upgrade no migration path. `Rounds.build` also changes character from a runner to a writer: it now re-validates the entire record through `save` (schema/round.schema.json is additionalProperties:false), so a record the current schema rejects makes `gbg round build` throw a RoundError instead of building. ARCHITECTURE §6.2 step 9, which enumerates close's preconditions, was not amended, so the documented contract and the code now disagree about what close requires.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE §6.2 step 9 (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1562-1570) still lists close's requirements as "the latest pass open_ids == [], no DEAD lane, every expected lane graded in that pass, config_sha and tool_version unchanged …, the round's existing files committed" with no mention of a recorded build. grep confirms rec["build"] is written at exactly one site, src/CLI/Rounds.jl:323.

findings.title: One rotted seed anchor now refuses the whole round where the round used to run with the rest planted
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:160-167 — the check-consistency refusal in prepare
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:245-256 — the check-docs refusal in seed_docs_corpus!
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:172 and src/CLI/Rounds.jl:297 — the reporting branches the refusals made unreachable
findings.before:
plan, skipped = Seeds.select(cat, f, rec["seed_salt"])
            f2, s2 = Seeds.plant(f, s, plan)
            write(full, f2); write(site, s2)
            println(io, "prepare: $(length(plan)) seed(s) planted …", isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): " * join(skipped, ", "))
findings.after:
if !isempty(skipped)
                println(io, "prepare: refused — $(length(skipped)) seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript: ", join(skipped, ", "))
                …
                return 2
            end
findings.why_it_matters: A consumer whose .gbg/seeds.toml has drifted by one class — the exact state 2026-09-12-check-docs-01 was in, where `count-drift`'s anchor "49 read-only checks" no longer occurred — can no longer prepare a seeded round at all. Before the commit that round ran, planted 5 of 6 classes and reported the sixth as skipped; after it, `gbg round prepare` exits 2 and the only documented way forward is `--no-seed`, which drops the seeding and with it the only non-self-reported dead-lane signal for the whole round. The remedy therefore trades an under-reported denominator for no measurement at all whenever the catalogue is one anchor stale, and the catalogue is the consumer's own file that drifts with every corpus edit.
findings.description: The stated defect is that a skipped class leaves recall UNDEFINED and quietly narrows the denominator. That is a reporting defect and admits a reporting remedy — record the skipped classes in ROUND.toml / the recall report and make them loud at grade. Turning it into a hard refusal at preflight is a wider edit: it blocks the round rather than the silent measurement, and it does so for both instruments at once. The edit also leaves two now-dead reporting branches behind (Rounds.jl:172, 297 still compose "; skipped classes (anchor absent): …" on a path where `skipped` is provably empty), which is the visible sign that the refusal was bolted in front of the reporting rather than replacing it.
findings.evidence: Rounds.jl:172 after the refusal: `println(io, "prepare: $(length(plan)) seed(s) planted (salt …)", isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): " * join(skipped, ", "))` — reachable only when `isempty(skipped)`, so the second branch can never print. src/CLI/Seed.jl:61 shows `skipped` is per-class anchor absence: `isempty(hits) && (push!(skipped, c["name"]); continue)`.

findings.title: source_globs repurposes latex_source_globs, narrowing the authored-source substrate for any consumer that set it
locations: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:726-731 — the resolution and the fallback
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/panel.js:86 — the substrate sentence
instruments/check-consistency/schema.json:25,169-176 — source_globs added to args.required
src/CLI/Passes.jl:588 and instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-state.js:21 — the same path list still hardcoded
findings.before: if (needs.includes('source')) parts.push(`ALSO the AUTHORED SOURCE …: the docstrings under ${A.repo}/src/ and ${A.repo}/ext/, the pages under ${A.repo}/docs/src/, and the rationale documents under ${A.repo}/docs/.`)
findings.why_it_matters: For a consumer that has NOT set the key the substrate is unchanged. For one that HAS, the hat's authored source is replaced, not extended: ARCHITECTURE's own worked configs set `latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]` (line 1241) and `["src/*.jl"]` (line 1353), so on the next panel a `needs: source` hat — latex-typesetter, doc-policy, naming-policy, invariants-and-decisions, fossil-and-drift — stops being pointed at docs/src/ pages, the docs/ rationale documents and ext/ altogether, while its persona still requires it to quote findings at their source file:line. That is the same class of silent unread surface the change was written to end, pointed the other way, and it lands on five hats at once. The key's name and its only documented appearances are LaTeX-flavoured; nothing in ARCHITECTURE or the config schema says it enumerates the whole authored-source corpus.
findings.description: Wiring a key that had no reader is right; overloading it as the definition of the whole authored-source substrate is wider than that, because the consumer wrote its value under the old meaning and gets a narrowed panel without being asked. A union (defaults plus the consumer's globs), or a new key, would have given the Literate surface its reader without taking anything away. The change is also only half-applied: `pass open` still hands the state verifier a hardcoded `source_scope` of ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"] (Passes.jl:588) and verify-state.js keeps the same literal as its fallback, so after this commit a consumer's panel hats and its state verifier read different corpora on the same round. Finally, `source_globs` is `required` in the instrument schema, so a round whose args were rendered by the previous CLI no longer validates against the current schema.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1241 `latex_source_globs   = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]` and :1353 `latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl"]`; schema/config.schema.json:441 defines the key as a bare `$ref: strlist` with `default: []` and no description binding it to the hat substrate; src/CLI/Passes.jl:588 `"source_scope" => ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"]`.

findings.title: The quantifier class enlarges every lane's mandatory claim checklist by a third to two fifths
locations: src/CLI/Preflight.jl:352-353 — CLAIM_QUANTIFIER and CLAIM_TOOL_ID
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:400-406 — the tagging conjunction
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:344 — the third CLAIM_EXIT alternative
catalog/lanes/check-docs.toml:12 — the brief that makes every item a debt
findings.before:
ex = occursin(CLAIM_EXIT, s)
            (ex || occursin(CLAIM_NUMBER, s)) || continue
            push!(out, "- [" * (ex ? "exit" : "count") * "] `$f:$n` — " * first(s, 220))
findings.after:
qu = occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, s) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, s)
            (ex || num || qu) || continue
            push!(out, "- [" * (ex ? "exit" : num ? "count" : "quantifier") * "] `$f:$n` — " * first(s, 220))
findings.why_it_matters: The checklist is not advisory: the lane brief says each item "is a claim you MUST discharge … one entry per item" and "an item you leave out of claims_checked[] reads as an item you did not check". Running both regex sets over the real corpus with the code's own predicate order, the src surface goes from 167 items to 227 (+36%), the docs surfaces from 1080 to 1507 (+425 items, +40%), instruments 58→69, policy 32→35. No cap, cost or budget moved in the same diff, so the same lane at the same economy strength now owes half again as many mechanical verdicts before its six checks begin — the affordability argument the comment itself invokes as the reason the class was dropped the first time. The likely outcome is not more claims checked but more items omitted, which the brief reads as unchecked.
findings.description: The class is worth having — two of five planted seeds were quantifier mutations and both were missed — and the conjunction with a tool identifier is a genuine narrowing from the 2526-line raw match. But the narrowing is looser than the comment's "a fraction of that" suggests, because CLAIM_TOOL_ID admits the bare phrase `gbg <word>` and CLAIM_QUANTIFIER admits `all`, `any` and `only`, which occur in ordinary prose on lines that merely mention a verb. A tighter identifier set, or a cap per surface, would have bought the seeded class without a 40% rise in mandatory items. Separately, the new CLAIM_EXIT alternative `\bexit\s+contract\b[^.]{0,60}?[0-3]\b` matches any digit 0-3 within 60 characters of the phrase, including the trailing digit of a larger number, so it can tag a line that states no exit code; one docs line already flips from `count` to `exit` in the measurement.
findings.evidence: Measured with the head and base regexes and the head predicate order over the tracked corpus (build trees excluded): `src old=167 new=227 added_by_quantifier=56`, `docs old=1080 new=1507 added_by_quantifier=425`, `instruments old=58 new=69`, `policy old=32 new=35`, `catalog old=9 new=9`. Brief, catalog/lanes/check-docs.toml: "Each one is a claim you MUST discharge … An item you leave out of `claims_checked[]` reads as an item you did not check."

findings.title: Admitting the open rounds to the release build also waives the gate's committed-without-the-round refusal
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:70 — admitted_rounds
src/CLI/Release.jl:167-169 — GBG_ROUND on the SELF.DOCS build
src/CLI/Gate.jl:82-88 — `r.name in ignored && continue` ahead of the :committed check
findings.why_it_matters: GBG_ROUND does not merely lift the open-round refusal for the named rounds: in gate_problems the `r.name in ignored && continue` short-circuit comes BEFORE the `:committed` check, so an admitted round is also exempt from "its files are untracked or modified while HEAD moved past the round's opening head — the fixes were committed without the round". An rc cut while a docs round is open therefore now passes its own SELF.DOCS step in a state the gate was written to refuse: round fixes committed without the round. Before this edit that release was refused outright, so the condition could never be reached; after it, it is reached and unchecked.
findings.description: Restoring the `if !rc` permission is correct — it had been unreachable for nine releases. The admission is broader than the permission needs: it hands the build the whole set of open docs rounds through a switch that suppresses every round-based refusal for them, rather than suppressing only the `:open` kind the release deliberately tolerates. GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP still guarantees a build that did not happen cannot pass, so the loss is confined to the committed-with-the-round guarantee, but that guarantee is exactly what protects a release cut in the middle of a fix pass.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Gate.jl:82-88: `r.name in ignored && continue` precedes `push!(problems, :open => …)` and the `if !in_ci && head !== nothing && head != r.round["head"]` block that raises `:committed`. src/CLI/Release.jl:70: `admitted_rounds(cfg) = join(frozen_rounds(cfg, Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS...), ",")` — every open docs round, unconditionally.

findings.title: gbg round scripts unfreezes a round's Workflow scripts mid-round, and its own docstring still says nothing does
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:338 — the docstring claim
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:346-354 — refresh_scripts, the second caller of copy_scripts
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:909, 924 — the usage line and the dispatch
schema/round.schema.json:238-261 — scripts_refreshed
findings.before: (no such verb; Preflight.copy_scripts was called only at src/CLI/Preflight.jl:928, inside preflight)
findings.why_it_matters: "Instruments are frozen mid-round" is one of this package's core invariants, and the freeze is what makes a round's scores comparable: the scripts that graded pass 1 are the scripts that grade pass 5. The new verb lets them move between passes, at the session's discretion, with the appended record as the only trace — so a reader of a closed round must now check `scripts_refreshed` before treating its passes as commensurable, and nothing in the round's own tally or in the protocol tells them to. Recording it is the right half of the remedy; what is missing is any statement of when a refresh is legitimate, and any refusal or warning when one lands between two graded passes rather than before the first.
findings.description: The motivating case is real — a round whose own finding is an unparseable verifier cannot verify itself, and the hand-fix that unblocked 2026-09-12-check-docs-01 left no trace at all. But the verb as written grants the unfreeze generally, for any round, at any point in its life, and the invariant it relaxes is documented nowhere as relaxed: the protocols and ARCHITECTURE still describe preflight as the moment the scripts are fixed. The new docstring is itself already false on this point — it asserts `copy_scripts` "runs there and nowhere else" in the body of the second function that runs it.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:338: "A round's scripts are FROZEN at preflight — [`Preflight.copy_scripts`](@ref) runs there and nowhere else" — while src/CLI/Rounds.jl:348 in the same function calls `Preflight.copy_scripts(cfg, String(rec["instrument"]), round)`; grep shows the two call sites, Preflight.jl:928 and Rounds.jl:348. CLAUDE.md core invariants: "Instruments are frozen mid-round."
